consent.title: Consent to take part
consent.body:
Your answers are recorded anonymously: the app never asks for your name, email or student id.
The data is used for discussion in class and to compare across classes. The instructor may use the anonymous data for research if you agree.
You take part fully whether you agree or not.

setup.orderHelp2: Default order from the plan; use ↑↓ to change it. Experiments split in two parts (such as E02) have two rows.
a.listHelp: Pick one box on every row. The confirm button unlocks once every row has a choice.
a.noAnswer: You did not answer this part.
a.youInconsistent: You switched back and forth more than once in the list, so there is no single switching point. Your answers are left out of the class median.
a.youCe: You switched from the gamble to the sure amount between {lo} and {hi} {unit}. Your certainty equivalent is about {ce} {unit}.
a.youRp: The gamble's expected value is {ev} {unit}, so your risk premium is about {rp} {unit}.
a.youAverse: Positive premium: you accept less than the expected value to avoid risk (risk averse).
a.youLoving: Negative premium: you need more than the expected value to give up the gamble (risk seeking).
a.youNeutral: Zero premium: you value the gamble at its expected value (risk neutral).
a.youViolate: This pair of choices is inconsistent with the independence axiom of expected utility theory.
a.youConsistent: This pair of choices is consistent with expected utility theory.
a.shareAverse: Share risk averse (certainty equivalent below expected value)
a.shareInconsistent: Share switching more than once (left out of the median)
a.ceDist: Certainty equivalent ({unit}); the expected value is {ev}
a.ceNote: {m} people who switched more than once are left out. Groups under 3 people are merged with a neighbour.
a.wtpDist: Willingness to pay for the St. Petersburg game ({unit})
a.wtpNote: The game's expected value is infinite. Median in this class: {med} {unit}; earlier classes: {prev} {unit}.
a.classicPattern: Chose {a} in problem 1 and {b} in problem 2 (the common violation)
a.anyViolation: All pairs violating the independence axiom
a.crossNote: Cross table of the {n} people who answered both problems. Red cells violate the independence axiom; the bold cell is the most common pattern. Percentages only.
a.ellsberg.k00: You chose the box with the known mix both times. No belief about the unknown box explains this pair, since that box cannot hold fewer tickets of the first colour and also fewer of the second. This is ambiguity aversion.
a.ellsberg.k11: You chose the box with the unknown mix both times. This pair does not fit any single belief either; it is ambiguity seeking.
a.ellsberg.k01: You chose the known box first and the unknown box second: consistent with believing the unknown box holds more tickets of the second colour.
a.ellsberg.k10: You chose the unknown box first and the known box second: consistent with believing the unknown box holds more tickets of the first colour.
a.ellsberg.classicPattern: Known box for both bets (ambiguity aversion)
a.ellsberg.anyViolation: Same box for both bets, in total (fits no single belief)
a.ellsberg.crossNote: Cross table of {n} people who answered both bets. Red cells: the same box both times, which fits no single belief; bold: ambiguity aversion. Shares only.
a.presentbias.k00: You took the sooner payment both times: consistent over time.
a.presentbias.k11: You waited both times: consistent over time.
a.presentbias.k01: You took the money today but were willing to wait when both payments were far away. Same week of waiting, same difference, opposite choice: this is present bias, which exponential discounting cannot explain.
a.presentbias.k10: You waited today but took the sooner payment when both were far away: a reversal in the opposite direction to present bias, which exponential discounting cannot explain either.
a.presentbias.classicPattern: Sooner in problem 1, later in problem 2 (present bias)
a.presentbias.anyViolation: People who reversed their choice between the two problems, in total
a.presentbias.crossNote: Cross table of {n} people who answered both problems. Red cells: choices that reverse when both dates move away; bold: present bias. Shares only.
c.lowHigh: Every question needs both bounds, and the lower bound cannot exceed the upper bound.
c.youHits: The true answer fell inside your range on {k} of {n} questions. A well-calibrated 90% range would score about {exp}.
c.youLambda: You need to win at least {g} {unit} to accept a risk of losing {l} {unit}. Your loss aversion coefficient: λ = {lam}.
c.lambdaAbove: λ above 1: a loss weighs more for you than a gain of the same size.
c.lambdaBelow: λ below 1: you accept the gamble even when the win is smaller than the loss.
c.lambdaOne: λ equal to 1: gains and losses of the same size weigh the same for you.
c.lambdaCapped: You entered the highest value allowed, so your true coefficient may be higher.
c.timedOut: Time ran out before you answered.
c.stroopYou: Your median response time: {c} ms when the word matched the ink, {i} ms when it did not.
c.stroopYouDelay: Your Stroop delay: {d} ms, that is {p}% slower when the word and ink conflicted.
c.stroopNoData: Not enough correct taps to compute your times.
c.stroopErrors: You tapped wrongly on {ei} of {ni} conflicting turns and {ec} of {nc} matching turns.
c.stroopExplain: When a word names one colour but is printed in another, reading the word happens almost automatically and gets in the way of naming the ink, so people slow down and make more mistakes.
c.stroopTitle: Stroop delay: how many milliseconds slower each person was when word and ink conflicted
c.stroopMedI: Median time, word conflicts with ink (ms)
c.stroopSlowerPct: Slower when word and ink conflict, median per person
c.stroopShareSlower: People slower when word and ink conflict
c.stroopNote: Per person: median time of correct taps; turns faster than {min} ms, slower than {max} ms or while the screen was left are dropped.
c.hitRate: Share of ranges containing the true answer
c.hitsDist: Questions whose true answer fell inside the 90% range (well calibrated: about {k} of {n})
c.lambdaDist: λ = minimum win divided by the loss of {l} {unit}; λ = 1 means no loss aversion
c.lambdaNote: {cap} people entered the highest value allowed. Groups under 3 people are merged with a neighbour.
